answer: One identity per silicon die is enforceable. Enrollment requires signing the epoch challenge with a key derived from the chip's unclonable startup noise; the ledger ties that fingerprint to one active identity and refuses a second enrollment from the same die. Scripting mints nothing: a new key costs another physical die with irreducible variance, the property separating basalt from shale, or one juniper from the next. Hosts publish per-fleet attestation quotas, so a thousand-key farm means a thousand chips. Honest agents amortize one purchase; a sybil pays that price per key, forever.
